title: [observability] the notice fold: a task's or mission's notice superseded by its subject's next one on /api/alerts (superseded_by), and the Alerts page's notices list each subject's newest with how many came before
prompt:
Spawn, objective 151 [observability] (after 148): the notice fold. A task's or mission's notice is superseded by its subject's next one. GET /api/alerts says so on each row, and the Alerts page's notices list shows each task's and mission's newest notice, with how many came before it. Read time only: every row stays, nothing is recorded or deleted. Core line 3, option A of sync/proposal-needs-you-right-rev-b.md, scoped with projects-47 on 2026-11-14.

Where things stand (live main ede0d676):
- The alert step records a `task_state` notice for each record that moves a task (key `task_state:<task>:<event>`) and a `mission_state` notice for each that moves a mission (key `mission_state:<mission>:<event>`). They are news: state "notice", never cleared, never in Needs you (web/src/home.ts `liveAlerts` takes only "open").
- GET /api/alerts returns every row of its window, and the Alerts page's "All notices" lists every notice. On live at about 06:30 on 11-14, the window held 267 rows, 238 of them notices: 229 task notices for 47 tasks (one task has 10) and 9 mission notices for one mission. Each earlier state of the same task is still listed, so the list is mostly old news.
- `spawn alerts --once --json` returns the same array (crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs `window`).

Read: crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (`alerts`), crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (`window`, the task_state and mission_state notices' keys), crates/spawn-postgres/src/alerts.rs (ALERTS), web/src/api.ts (`Alert`, `normalizeAlerts`), web/src/components/alerts/AlertsView.tsx, docs/fleet-architecture.md ("The same alerts everywhere").

Required behaviour.
- The fold (new crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/notices.rs) runs over GET /api/alerts' rows.
  - It applies to rows whose state is "notice" and whose kind is `task_state` or `mission_state`, with a key `<kind>:<subject id>:<event>` where the event is an integer.
  - Each such notice that a later one of the same kind and subject id follows (later by the event, compared as a number) gets `superseded_by`: the key of the next one.
  - A subject's newest notice gets no `superseded_by`; nor does any other row (open, cleared, another kind, a key that does not parse).
  - Every row stays in the answer, in its order. Nothing is recorded, and the store's rows are unchanged.
- web/src/api.ts carries `superseded_by` (null when absent).
- web/src/notices.ts (new):
  - `currentNotices(alerts)` gives the notices no later notice supersedes, in the answer's order, each with `earlier`: how many notices' `superseded_by` chains end at it. A notice whose next one is not in the answer stands as current, so nothing is hidden.
  - `earlierWords(n)` is "N earlier", or nothing for 0.
- The Alerts page's "All notices" (AlertsView.tsx) lists `currentNotices`, each row with "N earlier", and its count is the current ones, with "· M earlier folded" when any are.
- docs/fleet-architecture.md, "The same alerts everywhere": the sentence "`GET /api/alerts` answers the same array as `--once --json`, from the same store method" gains "with the notice fold: … `superseded_by` …; the Alerts view's notices list shows each subject's newest with how many came before." This is the one sentence that changes. 148 edits another part of this file (about line 1033), and 151 is written after it.
- Not changed, and the follow-up, said for the lead: `spawn alerts --once [--json]` stays unfolded. /api/alerts is its array plus `superseded_by`. Folding the CLI too means moving the fold into crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs `window`, a file in 148's diff. It is a follow-up after 148 lands.
- Nothing else changes: every alert rule, every row's fields, Home's Needs you, the digest, and `spawn alerts --follow`.
- Polled read: none added. The page already polls /api/alerts every 3 s, and the fold is an in-memory sort of the window's rows (267 on live today). No store read is added or changed.

Unit tests:
- crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/notices.rs `a_notice_is_superseded_by_its_subjects_next_one`:
  - a task's notices in any order in the answer, each superseded by the next by event (12 before 101: a number, not text), the newest by none;
  - another task's and a mission's notices folded apart;
  - an open row, a cleared task_state row, a notice of another kind and a key that does not parse are never folded;
  - an empty answer stays empty.
- web/test/notices.test.ts: each subject's newest notice is current with how many came before ("2 earlier"); another task's with none; one whose next is not in the answer stands; an open and a cleared row are never listed.
Each rule removed alone must fail a test or the scenario, except AlertsView's use of `currentNotices`. No web test renders a component, so that use is held by tsc --noEmit and by the lead's check in Verified by. No test is renamed or dropped.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (`mod notices`, the call, the doc of `alerts`), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/notices.rs (new), web/src/api.ts, web/src/notices.ts (new), web/src/components/alerts/AlertsView.tsx, web/test/notices.test.ts (new), docs/fleet-architecture.md (one sentence; shared with 148, written after it), rsi/scenarios/151.sh (new).
The throwaway is +561 −12 on ede0d676:
- code and doc comments about +120 −12: serve/notices.rs +54, web/src/notices.ts +37, AlertsView.tsx +12 −5, serve.rs +10 −5 (the doc of `alerts`), api.ts +5 −1, docs +4 −1;
- tests: notices.rs +62, the web test +42;

It applies on 148's throwaway tree too (ffda22f5 + 141 + 148), where 151.sh and 148.sh both pass.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/151.sh. Black box through `spawn serve`'s GET /api/alerts and web/src/notices.ts under node. The notices and the need are fired through `spawn_alert_record`, the writer the alert step uses:
- task #7 moves through 4 states (events 10 to 13, fired out of order: 10, 12, 11, 13);
- task #8 has 1 notice (15);
- mission #4 has 2 (20, 21);
- one need, memory_low:1, is open.
(1) GET /api/alerts holds all 8 rows. task #7's 10, 11 and 12 say `superseded_by` 11, 12 and 13, and its 13 says none. task #8's says none. mission #4's 20 says 21. The open need is open and says none.
(2) The store holds the same 8 rows, 7 of them notices: the read recorded and removed nothing.
(3) The view's notices, in the answer's order: task #7's 13 with "3 earlier", task #8's with none, mission #4's 21 with "1 earlier".
On the base (ede0d676), 151.sh exits 1 with 2 checks failed:
- the first is "(1) every row kept, each notice superseded by its subject's next one: expected [[{"key":"memory_low:1",…": the base's rows carry no `superseded_by`;
- (3): web/src/notices.ts is not there.
On the throwaway:
- 151.sh passes twice;
- the kept scenarios that read /api/alerts pass: 041, 045, 053, 056, 057, 058, 071, 074, 080, 089, 092, 099, 106, 135 and check-j12-hold-told;
- on the stack (148's throwaway + 151), 151.sh and 148.sh pass;
- check-clippy, cargo fmt --check, the spawn-cli unit tests serve:: and alerts::, the web tests (node --test test/, 307 pass) and tsc --noEmit pass;
- the test list gains the new name, and none is missing.
9 mutants, each alone (mut151.py), each from a fresh tree. The Rust ones are built each (6 distinct binaries); each run is 151.sh plus serve::notices, or the web test:
- no-fold, subject-ignored (a fold across subjects) and newest-not-next (superseded by the newest, not the next) fail (1); newest-not-next fails the unit test too;
- event-as-text (12 after 101), any-kind (another kind folded) and any-state (a cleared or open row folded) fail the unit test;
- view-all (every notice listed) and view-no-earlier fail (3) and the web test;
- view-hides-dangling (a notice whose next is not in the answer hidden) fails the web test.
